messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: inference-queue-prod backlog > 20k, p95 latency > 4s, autoscaler_alert (rule: queue_depth_high) — https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/12345
pd-bot: PagerDuty incident #RD-2025-813 assigned to @Jordan — page fired at 1767894320, escalation in 5m if unacked
Jordan: acked — I'm on it. seeing big spike in requests from a single tenant (tenant: video-transcribe), routing skewed to gpu-pool-east.
Maya: +1, looking at autoscaler logs now. quick check: how many pending pods?
Jordan: ~470 pods Pending, node autoscaler didn't add nodes. p95 token throughput dropped 60%.
Lee: looks like cloud quota limit hit for vCPU in us-east-1, requests to provider API are returning 403/QuotaExceeded. autoscaler retries repeatedly.
Arya: if quota is the blocker we can either request quota bump (slow) or manually spin nodes in the dedicated pool. recommend manual spin for immediate relief.
Maya: trying manual k8s scale to create room for pending pods. running `kubectl get pods -n inference | grep Pending | wc -l` returned 471.
Maya: running the scale command now:
```
kubectl scale --replicas=40 deployment/inference-workers -n inference
```
Jordan: scale command triggered but pods are still Pending. node-provision shows errors: `FailedScheduling: 0/0 nodes are available: Insufficient cpu`.
Lee: confirmed cloud API error when provisioning nodes: `RequestLimitExceeded` then `QuotaExceeded`. That explains no new nodes.
Jordan: Ok — plan A: evict noncritical batch jobs (priorityClass=low) to free up CPU for inference workers. Plan B: enable fallback routing to smaller model (cpu-optimized) for non-SLAs. Plan C: notify Support and customers.
Arya: evicting batch jobs now — using the eviction script to target namespace `batch-jobs`. running:
```
kubectl delete pod -l job_type=batch -n batch-jobs --grace-period=0 --force
```
Lee: eviction started, helpers: watch node pressure and queue depth. I'll flip routing after we see freed nodes.
Maya: queue depth dropped from 22k -> 11k after evictions, p95 latency down to ~2.6s, still elevated.
Jordan: good. I'm going to route non-essential traffic to cpu-fallback pool. Applying quick policy change in routing service.
Jordan: policy patch applied: `route: inference-queue-prod -> fallback-model-cpu` for tenant list {video-transcribe} where SLA != gold.
SupportBot: Notifying impacted customers: support ticket auto-created for tenants: video-transcribe, livestream-inc, captionly (ticket ids SR-7654, SR-7655, SR-7656).
Arya: also enabling dedicated burst nodes — flipping reserved capacity to +10 instances for dedicated pool. should help with steady throughput.
Lee: monitoring cloud quotas; moved some ephemeral workloads to another region to free up vCPU usage (us-west-2). provider quota usage dropped ~18%.
Maya: autoscaler controller logs show it was stuck WAITING_FOR_QUOTA, I filed a follow-up to make it more resilient to quota errors: create backoff + fallback to manual-provision mode.
Jordan: customer impact summary so far: brief failures for some requests (5-10% error rate) over 12 minutes, overall latency increase for most tenants. No data leaks. Major customers with gold SLA unaffected due to reserved capacity.
Arya: filing a post-incident item: autoscaler should surface quota errors earlier and try alternate regions. ticket INFRA-2042 created.
Lee: short-term mitigation complete, queue back to 3k and p95 ~1.4s. I'll continue to monitor for 30m.
Jordan: handing off to next oncall @Maya in 20m. leaving runbook notes: 1) if Pending pods persist, check cloud vCPU quota and pre-provision nodes, 2) evict batch low-priority jobs, 3) enable fallback routing for non-critical tenants, 4) increase dedicated burst capacity.
Maya: taking over. I'll keep the thread updated. Thanks all :thumbsup:
pd-bot: PagerDuty incident #RD-2025-813 acknowledged by Jordan at 1767894330 and resolved at 1767894635 (status: mitigated).
Jordan: resolved for now. follow-ups: INFRA-2042 (autoscaler resilience), OPS-2043 (quota playbook), COMM-2044 (support customer comms). tagging owners in the tickets.
Maya: logging timeline and metrics to the incident doc: https://docs.internal/incidents/RD-2025-813 — will add graphs (queue depth, p95 latency, node count) and the exact commands used.
Jordan: thanks team, closing the live page. if anything spikes, re-open this thread or page oncall.
